scope: Proposition 5.2 (Integrality and traces) of the manuscript “Exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank” (preprints/Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from-Low-Selmer-Corank-October-7-2026/exact-bsd-low-selmer-corank.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 002 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 64b46603e174462e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The classes just constructed are integral away from pn2∞ and compatible with division traces and with corestriction as the p-part of M grows with A, c, d, ξ fixed. If ℓ ∤ cdn2L0 is a fresh prime and is adjoined to both orders and the root index, the rational norm multiplier is 1 − aℓ(f)[ℓ] ℓ + [ℓ]2 ℓ , (5.3) where [ℓ] sends the determinant root to its ℓ-th power. For qa 0 ∥ b, q0 ∤ b1, filling qa 0 into the first row gives, at a finite even character ν, zfilled = (1 − aq0 (f)ν(q0)/q0)zbefore. (5.4) The trace maps themselves are integral in both assertions.
